faq.heading: FAQs About Removing Gemini Watermarks
faq.intro: Answers about removing the visible Gemini watermark from saved images, limited free image uses, image quality, Nano Banana, and Google’s watermark settings.

items.question: How do I remove a Gemini watermark from an image?
items.answer: Upload the original JPG, PNG, or WebP image to WatermarkGemini and sign in with Google. Review the cost before processing, start the cleanup, then compare the returned JPG with your original. Inspect the former watermark area at full size before downloading. This workflow is for visible marks on images you own or have permission to edit; it does not remove invisible provenance information.

items.question: Can I remove a Gemini watermark online?
items.answer: Yes. WatermarkGemini provides a browser-based workflow for supported still images. You can select an image, sign in, review its processing cost, inspect the returned result, and download an edited JPG without installing a desktop photo editor. However, the selected file is uploaded to private processing storage when you prepare the task, so the service is not entirely local to your device.

items.question: Is Gemini Watermark Remover free to use?
items.answer: Eligible standard image processing includes limited free uses: one on first sign-in and one added through daily check-in, up to a free-use balance of three. The workspace displays the cost and available allowance before you run a task. This is not unlimited free processing. The pricing page currently says new purchases are paused; check the latest on-screen availability rather than assuming a paid plan can be purchased.

items.question: How do I turn off the visible watermark in Google Gemini?
items.answer: For newly generated content in Gemini Apps, open Settings → Media watermark at gemini.google.com and switch off visible watermarks if your account is eligible. Availability can depend on location and plan. This setting applies to new Gemini Apps media, not images you already downloaded, and it does not disable SynthID or Content Credentials. See Google’s official help and our guide to turning off Gemini watermarks.

items.question: Does this work on Nano Banana images and other Gemini marks?
items.answer: Nano Banana belongs to Google’s Gemini image-generation family, but not every export has the same visible mark. WatermarkGemini is intended for supported visible image watermarks, and the result depends on the particular file, mark, and background. Try an authorized image and inspect the preview rather than assuming every variant will be removed. For more specific model information, see our Nano Banana Watermark Remover page.

items.question: Can I remove a Gemini watermark without cropping?
items.answer: Yes. WatermarkGemini processes the visible watermark area rather than removing part of the frame. This helps keep the image dimensions, composition, and edge details that would otherwise be lost to cropping. It is still a visual edit, so check the cleaned region for artifacts, especially over textured backgrounds or important subjects.

items.question: Will removing a Gemini watermark reduce image quality?
items.answer: Results depend on watermark size, location, and the details behind it. WatermarkGemini aims to make the cleaned region blend with its surroundings, but fine texture can change and the output JPG may have different compression from your source image. Compare both versions at 100% zoom and keep the original. No tool can guarantee identical pixels or a perfect result in every case.

items.question: Which image formats are supported?
items.answer: The Gemini image workflow accepts one JPG, PNG, or WebP image up to 10 MB at a time and currently returns a JPG. Start with the original Gemini export when possible. Screenshots, heavily compressed re-saves, or unusually placed marks can make cleanup harder to evaluate. The separate site-wide uploader also lists MP4, but video jobs use a different workspace and processing rules.

items.question: Do I need to sign in before removing a watermark?
items.answer: Yes. You can select and preview a file locally first, but Google sign-in is required to prepare and process it. After sign-in, the workspace may upload the selected file to validate it and calculate the processing cost before you click the final processing action. Do not upload confidential material without reviewing the Privacy Policy and the processing-provider terms.

items.question: Does this tool remove Google’s invisible SynthID watermark?
items.answer: No. WatermarkGemini targets visible image marks, such as the Gemini sparkle. SynthID is a separate invisible watermark used by Google, and Content Credentials are another provenance signal. Removing a visible corner logo does not remove those signals or change how the image was created. Keep appropriate AI-origin disclosures when sharing edited media.

items.question: Why does my Gemini image still show a watermark after changing settings?
items.answer: Turning off Media watermark in Gemini Apps affects newly created eligible content; it does not go back and rewrite files you already saved. The setting may also be unavailable for some accounts or locations, and it does not control every Google AI product. For an existing image, you can regenerate it with the setting off or review a permitted visible-mark cleanup with WatermarkGemini. Neither approach removes SynthID.
